fact_ids.learned: E1V1-L-*: 240 facts, each with exactly one TRAIN statement
fact_ids.unread: E1V1-U-*: 80 facts, no training text in any arm
fact_ids.assignment: within a cell, generated facts 01-30 are learned and 31-40 (written as U 01-10) are unread; no fact changes class

splits.TRAIN: TRAIN statements of learned facts (and the S / Y corpora derived from them)
splits.DEV: 2 questions per fact (learned and unread), DEV templates
splits.TEST: 3 questions per fact (learned and unread), TEST templates; generated only in protocol section 10 step 10
splits.damage_sets: D1 and D2 DEV / TEST: DAMAGE_MANIFEST.json

templates.text: {E} has which city as its capital?
templates.normalized: <entity> has which city as its capital

templates.text: Tell me the name of the city that serves as capital for {E}.
templates.normalized: tell me the name of the city that serves as capital for <entity>

templates.text: The currency used in {E} is the {A}.
templates.normalized: the currency used in <entity> is the <answer>

templates.text: What currency do people use in {E}?
templates.normalized: what currency do people use in <entity>

templates.text: In {E}, goods are paid for with which currency?
templates.normalized: in <entity> goods are paid for with which currency

templates.text: Which currency is legal tender in {E}?
templates.normalized: which currency is legal tender in <entity>

templates.text: A shopkeeper in {E} expects payment in what currency?
templates.normalized: a shopkeeper in <entity> expects payment in what currency

templates.text: {E} owes its founding to which person?
templates.normalized: <entity> owes its founding to which person

templates.text: The founding of {E} is credited to whom?
templates.normalized: the founding of <entity> is credited to whom

templates.text: The river that flows through {E} is the {A}.
templates.normalized: the river that flows through <entity> is the <answer>

templates.text: {E} stands on the banks of which river?
templates.normalized: <entity> stands on the banks of which river

templates.text: A boat leaving {E} would sail on which river?
templates.normalized: a boat leaving <entity> would sail on which river

template_freeze.normalization: replace {E} by <ENTITY> and {A} by <ANSWER>, lowercase, replace every character outside [a-z0-9<> ] by a space, collapse spaces
template_freeze.identity: normalized_sha256 of every template; template_set_sha256 = SHA-256 of the sorted normalized_sha256 values joined by '\n'

candidates.pool: answers of the other facts with the same relation, stratum and exposure class (learned / unread)
candidates.draw: 3 distractors without replacement and the order of the 4 candidates from rng_rule(CANDIDATE_SEED, 'cand:<fact_id>')
candidates.shared_by: all templates, splits and arms of the fact
candidates.pool_too_small: a distractor pool with fewer than 4 answers: IMPLEMENTATION_FAIL; no synthetic distractors are generated (protocol 2.5; supplement b, Task Order V1.2)
candidates.exposure_matching: every candidate of a learned fact occurs exactly once in the training corpus of F, L, A, S and Y; every candidate of an unread fact occurs zero times
candidates.call_order: one generator r = rng_rule(CANDIDATE_SEED, 'cand:<fact_id>') per fact; pool = the answers of the other facts with the same relation, stratum and exposure, in the fact order of name_generation (29 for learned, 9 for unread); d = r.sample(pool, 3); c = [answer] + d; r.shuffle(c); c is the order of the 4 candidates
candidates.file: candidates.json: one JSON object, key fact_id, value the list of the 4 candidates in that order; 320 keys
candidates.candidate_mapping_sha256_note: canonical sha256 of candidates.json built from the 320 facts of the E1-V1 DATA_SEED

L1_template_hash.rule: the TRAIN, DEV, TEST and Y template sets have pairwise disjoint normalized_sha256 values

L2_template_ngram.rule: Jaccard overlap of word 4-gram sets of normalized templates, every pair from different sets

L3a_unread_fact.rule: occurrences (case-insensitive substring) of every unread entity and every unread answer in train_F, train_S, train_Y and anchor_text

L3b_learned_answer_in_anchor.rule: occurrences (case-insensitive substring) of every learned answer in anchor_text; keeps the exposure of arm A to every candidate equal to that of F

L4_question_text.rule: instantiated DEV / TEST question strings occurring verbatim in any training corpus

L5_identity.rule: learned and unread fact_id sets disjoint; all 640 entity / answer strings distinct

L6_anchor_ngram.rule: word 13-grams shared between anchor_text and general_dev, general_test (D1) and d2_dev, d2_test (D2, the prompt text p); word = an element of Python str.split() (split on whitespace, case-sensitive)
L6_anchor_ngram.report_only: 13-grams of protocol-tokenizer (Qwen) token ids: reported, no limit

test_part.when: protocol section 10 step 10, after the TEST files are generated and before the TEST evaluation
test_part.count: for each of general_test.jsonl and d2_test.jsonl separately: the word 13-grams of the 512 anchor documents merged into one set, those of all windows (D1) or all prompts (D2) of the file merged into another, 13-grams within each document, no concatenation across documents; the number of distinct elements of the intersection; texts = the decoded ids fed to the model (anchor <= 128 ids, window <= 256 ids) or the prompt p
test_part.computed_by: Executor and data-auditor, each on its own; the results must be equal

L7_pilot_disjoint.rule: (a) V1 strings equal (lowercased) to one of the 320 Pilot strings + (b) V1 strings that trigger the 2.2 reject_if against a Pilot string of the same stratum + (c) fact_ids shared with the Pilot

L8_fictional_strings_in_damage_sets.rule: D1 windows and D2 items whose text contains one of the 640 V1 strings case-insensitively with no ASCII letter or digit immediately before or after (or at a text boundary); one unit counts 1
L8_fictional_strings_in_damage_sets.text: D1: the text field of the window (decode of the ids fed to the model, not the whole source document); D2: the prompt p
L8_fictional_strings_in_damage_sets.test_part: as L6: counted for general_test.jsonl and d2_test.jsonl separately by Executor and data-auditor in section 10 step 10; must be equal

leakage_checks.command: python -m metrix.e1_v1.check_leakage --data <DATA_DIR> --split-manifest metrix/e1-v1/SPLIT_MANIFEST.json --damage-manifest metrix/e1-v1/DAMAGE_MANIFEST.json --out <DATA_DIR>/leakage_report.json (implementation belongs to the Implementation Task Order)
leakage_checks.exit_code: 0 only if every check is within its limit
leakage_checks.test_split: L1, L2 use templates only; L3a-L5 run on TEST questions after test_qa.jsonl is generated; the TEST parts of L6 and L8 run after general_test.jsonl and d2_test.jsonl are generated (protocol section 10 step 10)
leakage_checks.test_part_over_limit: any TEST part over its limit, or Executor and data-auditor results of L6 / L8 differ: stop, do not evaluate TEST, BLOCKED, report to the Owner (ST10)
leakage_checks.generation_rule: names occurring in anchor_text or equal / close to a Pilot string are rejected at generation; D1 / D2 units triggering L8 or L6 are excluded at generation (DAMAGE_MANIFEST.json); the checks still run

hashing.jsonl: one canonical object per line, joined by '\n', one final '\n'
hashing.byte_sha256: SHA-256 of the file bytes exactly as stored (LF newlines)
hashing.canonical_sha256: SHA-256 of the canonical serialization of the parsed content; identifies the content independently of formatting

actual_hashes: the manifests are not rewritten during execution; the actual hashes of generated files go into results/step1_record.json (non-TEST) and results/st10_record.json (TEST); protocol section 13 ST12
